basic_information.short_title: Renaming of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat to West Upi
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT RENAMING THE MUNICIPALITY OF DATU BLAH T. SINSUAT, MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE TO MUNICIPALITY OF WEST UPI, MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Renames the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat in Maguindanao del Norte to the Municipality of West Upi — subject to approval by its own voters in a plebiscite.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act states a policy of genuine and meaningful local autonomy so that subdivisions can develop as self-reliant communities. It gives no separate reason for the change of name itself.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: If ratified, the municipality carries a geographic name rather than one honouring an individual. Nothing else about its territory, government or status changes.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of the municipality, who vote on the change
Anyone holding documents, records or addresses in the municipality's name
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: The act is in force, but the renaming happens only on ratification by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: You decide. The Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat becomes the Municipality of West Upi — but only if a majority of votes cast by its own voters approve it in a plebiscite.
in_practice: The name changes from Datu Blah T. Sinsuat to West Upi
Ratification requires a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters of the municipality
COMELEC conducts and supervises the plebiscite under paragraph (g), Section 13 of the Local Government Code of 1991
Plebiscite costs are charged to the Contingent Fund of the Office of the Chief Minister
Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 198, which created the municipality, is amended accordingly

for_specific_groups.Residents: Only voters of this municipality decide — the vote is confined to the unit whose name changes, which is also the only unit affected.
for_specific_groups.Anyone with records in the old name: The act sets no transition arrangements for documents, addresses, signage or registrations.
for_specific_groups.Businesses and offices: No compliance duty is created, but the municipality's legal name would change on ratification.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte.
what_you_can_do: Vote in the plebiscite — a majority of votes cast decides
Ask COMELEC when it is scheduled; the act sets no deadline
watch_out_for: The act sets no deadline for holding the plebiscite, unlike the municipality-creation acts which specify 60 days.
No transition provisions are made for records, addresses or signage in the old name.
The act gives no stated reason for the change of name.

key_terms_explained.Plebiscite: A vote of the people affected, required here before the renaming takes effect.
key_terms_explained.Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 198: The law of the former ARMM that created the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat, amended by this act.
key_terms_explained.Local Government Code of 1991: Republic Act 7160; its Section 13(g) governs the conduct of plebiscites on changes of name.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhul Hijjah 02, 1447 / 19 May 2026, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 21 May 2026.

benefits.headline: A change of municipal name, put to the municipality's own voters.

direct_benefits.benefit: A direct vote on the name of your municipality
direct_benefits.how_to_access: At the plebiscite conducted by COMELEC

indirect_benefits: A geographic name in place of one honouring an individual
limitations: Nothing changes without a favourable plebiscite.
No deadline is set for holding it.
No transition arrangements for records in the old name.

for_citizens: None beyond voting in the plebiscite, which is a right rather than a duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections (COMELEC), which conducts and supervises the plebiscite
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A resident votes in the plebiscite on whether their municipality is renamed West Upi. A majority of the votes cast decides it.
A business registered in the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat would, on ratification, sit in the Municipality of West Upi. The act says nothing about how existing registrations are updated.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Renames the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat in the Province of Maguindanao del Norte as the Municipality of West Upi, Maguindanao del Norte.

Section 2 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Government declares that its territorial and political subdivisions shall enjoy genuine and meaningful local autonomy, to attain their fullest development as self-reliant communities and become more effective partners in attaining regional development goals.

Section 3 — The renaming is subject to ratification by a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters of the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat in a plebiscite conducted for the purpose. The Commission on Elections conducts and supervises it in compliance with paragraph (g), Section 13 of Republic Act 7160, the Local Government Code of 1991. Expenses are charged against the Contingent Fund of the Office of the Chief Minister.

Section 4 — Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 198, creating the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat, is amended accordingly, and inconsistent laws, orders, rules and regulations are repealed, modified, superseded or amended.
Section 5 — Takes effect 15 days after complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM.

impact.allocated_budget: Plebiscite expenses charged to the Contingent Fund of the Office of the Chief Minister; no amount stated.

related_legislation.related_note: Amends the former ARMM law that created the municipality. The same namesake appears in BAA 25, which upgraded the Datu Blah Sinsuat District Hospital.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The renaming depends on ratification in a plebiscite; whether that plebiscite has been held is not recorded here.

citizen_questions.a: Not automatically. The change takes effect only on ratification by a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters of the municipality in a plebiscite.
Qualified voters of the Municipality of Datu Blah T. Sinsuat. The vote is confined to the municipality whose name would change.
The act does not set a deadline — unlike the municipality-creation acts, which require a plebiscite within 60 days.
The Contingent Fund of the Office of the Chief Minister. No amount is stated.

citizen_questions.q: What happens to documents in the old name?
citizen_questions.a: The act is silent. It makes no transition provision for records, addresses, signage or registrations.
